problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$

feedback.problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=u-{e}^{v}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-{e}^{v}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-{e}^{v}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -{e}^{v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -{e}^{v}\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -{e}^{v}\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,{e}^{v},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
